paragraphs.text: Relay messages between agent harness's native sessions
# Agent Relay

Durable, bidirectional messaging between native agent sessions, shipped as a
DeepSeek Harness bundle

(`dsh-agent-relay-plugin`): DSH sessions and Codex threads
exchange messages with push delivery, th

read discovery, and delegated work that
returns to the conversation that asked.

A live DSH agent (a real DSH Web session) and a persistent native Codex thread
exchange durable mess

ages. Each side reaches the relay the way that harness is
supposed to be reached: DSH through a regi

stered `relay_send` tool whose sender
is taken from `exec.agent`, and Codex through a member-bound s

tdio MCP companion
whose sender is taken from its bearer credential.
## Install

Agent Relay is a DSH bundle. Installing it adds a **disabled** Host row to a
profile; enabling that

row in the profile's user layer starts the relay with every
boot of the profile.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Add the enable block to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (a top-level
YAML array). A later
layer replaces a row's whole `config`, so repeat every key:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Defaults: `teamId: relay`, `bridgePort: 33120`, journal at
`$DSH_HOME/agent-relay/journal.jsonl`, st

atus/log beside it, and lazy attachment
to the default Codex daemon socket when no transport is conf

igured. Restart the
profile: the relay starts with it and attaches to Codex whenever the daemon
appe
ars, even if that is after the host booted.
### Codex side

Codex reaches the relay through the bundled MCP companion. Add to
`~/.codex/config.toml`, using the
same token as the external member:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Create the member token file and install the skill into both harnesses:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Check that the layer composed without booting, then restart the profile:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Uninstall: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-agent-relay-plugin`.
## Compatibility and verification
| Component | Verified against |

| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.0-rc.2`; `engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0` |
| Codex CLI | `0.163.0`
— stdio app-server, WebSocket app-server, and the shared daemon's unix WebSocket endpoint; the proto

col was first probed on `0.162.1` |
| Node | `>=22` |

Verified end to end inside a real `web` profile: push delivery in both
directions, `relay_threads` d

iscovery, lazy attach when the Codex daemon starts
after the host, delegated work returning to the o

riginating Codex conversation,
and the relay's own ephemeral thread staying out of the user's histor

conversation,
and the relay's own ephemeral thread staying out of the user's history. See
Evidence.
## How it is wired (and what stays untouched)

The development profile `relay-dev` is created from the shipped `web` template
inside a **separate D

SH home** (`$PWD/.relay-home/dsh`), and the plugin is added
as an extra patch overlay for that boot

me** (`$PWD/.relay-home/dsh`), and the plugin is added
as an extra patch overlay for that boot only:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The user's real `~/.dsh` profile, sessions and credentials are never modified:
the isolated home bor

rows the credentials file by symlink and the overlay lives
in this workspace. `cordis.patch.yml` is

the same plugin as a proper bundle
layer, with its row **disabled by default** so installing the bun

dle alone
changes nothing until an operator enables it with a config.
### Using it with the real environment (`web-relay`)

A second instance runs inside the user's own `~/.dsh`, so it uses their real
credentials, models and

session history. It is a **new** profile created from the
shipped web template plus a copy of their

own patch layer; their `web` profile
is untouched.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Notes for that instance:

- It keeps its own journal and Codex home (`relay-personal`, `codex-personal`),
so it never contends

with the isolated `relay-dev` instance.
- It shares `~/.dsh/storages` and `~/.dsh/sessions` with an

y other running host
on the same home. Two hosts are fine for reading history; keep heavy
workspace/

registry edits in one host at a time.
- `dev/web-relay.patch.yml` pins `agent-default-model` to a re

achable model
because the profile's own selection (`pai`, `127.0.0.1:30808`) was not
reachable when

it was booted. Remove that block or switch model in the GUI
once that endpoint is up.
- Only session

s live **in that host** can be borrowed as members; sessions from
the other host appear in its histo
ry and can be resumed there.
### Connecting a Codex you run yourself (pull path)

The relay drives its own managed Codex. A Codex **you** run — your TUI, your IDE
session, your daemo
n — is reached the other way round: it pulls.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then give that Codex the relay MCP server (its own `~/.codex/config.toml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart that Codex (or reload its config) and it gains `relay_send`,
`relay_inbox`, `relay_members`,
`relay_status`. Semantics:

- Messages addressed to the external member stay **`queued`** — nothing is
injected into a process t

he relay does not own — and they survive relay
restarts.
- `relay_inbox` hands them over **exactly o

nce**; the relay then records
`accepted` with `receipt.deliveredBy: "pull"`.
- Recipients are resolv

ed, not required verbatim: `relay_members` lists every
member with an alias, its title and cwd (for

DSH sessions), and `to` accepts an
alias, any unique id prefix, or the full member id. Ambiguity and

unknown names
fail with the candidate list instead of guessing.
- Members can create new sessions w

hen the operator enables it
(`allowSessionCreation`, capped by `maxSpawnedMembers`): `relay_create_s

ession`
opens a fresh root DSH session in a chosen directory, or an additional
persistent Codex thre

ad, and can hand it its first task through the ordinary
relay path. DSH sessions are created through

the host's session controller, so
preset and model resolve before the first turn; `dshAgentPreset`

overrides the
preset.
- The external Codex can `relay_send` to any member; the DSH side is woken
nor

mally.
- Push into a thread another Codex process is currently holding is **not**
supported; that ne
eds the still-unimplemented daemon/control-socket attachment.

Verified end to end: `evidence/unmanaged-codex-pull.txt`, reproducible with
`node tools/unmanaged-co

dex-pull.mjs --url <bridge url> --token <token>`.
Copy-paste prompts for the Codex side (TUI and `co

dex exec`) are in
`examples/from-codex.md`.
